solution: LHS \(= \tan(3x - \pi/4) = \sqrt{3}\) gives \(3x = n\pi + \frac{7\pi}{12}\), i.e. \(x = \frac{n\pi}{3} + \frac{7\pi}{36}\). So \(p=3, q=36\), \(\frac{p}{q}=\frac{3}{36}=\frac{1}{12}\). Matches option B.

solution:
\(\cos\theta\cos 2\theta = \sin\theta\sin 2\theta\) gives \(\cos 3\theta = 0\), so \(\theta = \dfrac{(2k + 1)\pi}{6}\).

The values with \(\cos\theta = 0\) (\(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)) make \(\sin 2\theta = 0\), so \(\cot 2\theta\) is undefined and they are excluded. What remains is \(\theta = n\pi \pm \dfrac{\pi}{6}\).
note: at cos t = 0, cot 2t is undefined (sin 2t = 0), the product is not 0

solution: Converting: \(\sin^{-1}\frac{4}{5} = \tan^{-1}\frac{4}{3}\), \(\sin^{-1}\frac{5}{13} = \tan^{-1}\frac{5}{12}\). Their sum = \(\tan^{-1}\frac{63}{16}\). Then \(\sin^{-1}\frac{16}{65}=\tan^{-1}\frac{16}{63}\), which adds to the sum to give total = \(\frac{\pi}{2}\). So expression = \(2\pi - \frac{\pi}{2} = \frac{3\pi}{2}\). Matches option D.

solution: Adding the three: \(2(a+b+c)=24k\), so \(a+b+c=12k\). Then \(a=12k-(b+c)=4k\), \(b=12k-(c+a)=3k\), \(c=12k-(a+b)=5k\): a 3-4-5 triangle, right-angled, with area \(\frac12\cdot 3k\cdot 4k=6k^2\). So \(\dfrac{(A(\triangle ABC))^2}{k^4}=36\). Matches option (a).
note: 2(a+b+c)=24k gives a+b+c=12k (s would be 6k); the later lines use 12k as the sum; em dash replaced by a colon

solution: For \(hxy+gx+fy+c=0\): using the condition \(\Delta=0\) for the general second-degree equation with \(A=B=0\): \(\begin{vmatrix}0&h/2&g/2\\h/2&0&f/2\\g/2&f/2&c\end{vmatrix}=0\). Expanding determinant with \(A=0,B=0,C=c,F=f/2,G=g/2,H=h/2\): gives \(\dfrac{fgh}{4}-\dfrac{ch^2}{4}=0\), so \(fg=ch\) as \(h\neq0\). Matches option A.

solution: Principal values: \(\tan^{-1}(-\sqrt{3}) = -\dfrac{\pi}{3}\) (range \((-\pi/2, \pi/2)\)); \(\sin^{-1}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\) (range \([-\pi/2, \pi/2]\)); \(\cos^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\) (range \([0, \pi]\)). Sum \(= -\dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{2\pi}{3} = \dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{4\pi - 3\pi}{12} = \dfrac{\pi}{12}\). Matches option C: \(\dfrac{\pi}{12}\).

solution: For \(A\cos x + B\sin x = C\) with two distinct roots on the principal half-cycle, the standard half-angle identity gives \(\tan\!\left(\dfrac{\alpha+\beta}{2}\right) = \dfrac{B}{A}\). Here \(A = \sqrt{3}\,a\), \(B = 2b\), and \(\alpha+\beta = \pi/3\), so \(\tan(\pi/6) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{2b}{\sqrt{3}\,a}\). Cross-multiplying: \(\sqrt{3}\,a = 2b\sqrt{3}\), i.e. \(a = 2b\), so \(\dfrac{b}{a} = \dfrac{1}{2} = 0.5\). Matches option B: \(0.5\).
